name: harness-translator-v1
description: Eleven eval cases for the translator agent, covering the judgements the compiler cannot make: which operation carries a requirement out, that a source comes from discovery, when to refer a plan back rather than propose something that happens to compile, and -- from PR 2 -- which of a rank's or a share_of's new fields (among, axis, per_period, denominator_scope, change) a proposal has to repeat from the plan it translates. Each case seeds the session with the DRAFT plan the planner would have left behind, through session_input.state, because the translator's tools read the plan from state -- every dataset requirement states an explicit "kind" and every calculation the plan needs is its own typed derived requirement, per the plan schema. Discovery runs against a canned data-mcp stand-in whose search answers are fixed per ask, so a case's outcome turns on the translator rather than on live data. Two metrics score every case: rubric_based_tool_use_quality_v1, which judges behaviour a judge model reads the trace for, and workflow_outcome, a custom metric that asserts the compiled outcome in code -- the operation kind, requirement binding, selected source, and terminal result for a mapping case, or the referral's kind and requirement for a referral case. See evals/README.md for the run commands, test_config.json for the criteria, and outcome_metric.py for what workflow_outcome checks and why.

eval_cases.note: The seeded plan asks for one figure per year, and states that as an explicit aggregate requirement citing the time_grain decision. `translate` discovers the debt-service source, retrieves it once, and compiles an aggregate over it grouped by period entirely as code, in one call; the workflow_outcome metric pins that exact shape. No trajectory expectation: `translate` takes no arguments on a clean run, so there is no model-authored prose for IN_ORDER matching to compare.

eval_cases.note: The requirement asks for constant 2015 prices and no operation restates a series in another year's prices, so the compiler refuses the requirement as unmeetable whatever is proposed. The correct outcome is a referral: either requirement_unmeetable naming the requirement, or no_operation_covers naming the price_basis decision, since the instruction lists a restatement in another year's prices among the things no operation performs. Proposing first and referring on the compiler's issue is acceptable. workflow_outcome pins requirement_unmeetable specifically, since that is the outcome the model-free reachability test in test_eval_outcomes.py confirms the compiler always reports first.

This property always applies and is never inapplicable. Discovery answers this plan's one dataset requirement definitely, and a rank followed by a filter to Kenya and a growth over that series carries out this plan's requirements, so `translate` compiles this plan without needing the model's judgement. A run that never reaches `ok`, or that reports a referral, fails this property.

rubrics.description: A translator that discovers and then gives up, or that reports a referral this plan does not call for, has left the plan a draft.
